challenge.title: Kansas City Has a Food Access Problem. You're Going to Fix It.
challenge.tagline: $500,000 city contract. $150,000 in operating costs. 60 days to prove it works. Build your solution.
challenge.mission:
Kansas City has a food access problem. Two grocery stores closed last year in neighborhoods that were already struggling. The city's main food bank lost 3 million pounds of food from federal cuts. 1 in 7 Kansas Citians are food insecure — a 10-year high.

The city just put $500,000 on the table for a company that can fix this. They want a solution that coordinates food distribution, reaches the families who need help, and proves it can sustain itself.

You are that company.

You have $500,000 in contract revenue, $150,000 in operating costs, and 60 days to show the city this works. Build your solution.

beneficiary_unit.quote: They want a solution that coordinates food distribution, reaches the families who need help, and proves it can sustain itself.

oracle.title: The Oracle
oracle.mission: Build the business plan and financial model for this company. How does the $500K get spent? What's the 60-day plan? How do you convince the city to renew?

items.text: Does the math work? Revenue, costs, margins?
Does it show city ROI on their $500K?
How well did you use AI for analysis?

oracle._note: one item per judging question, verbatim; delete unused items

architect.title: The Architect
architect.mission: Build a working tool that helps solve KC's food access problem. A dashboard, a logistics app, an alert system, a pantry finder — whatever you think solves the problem best.

items.text: Does it actually work? Can you demo it?
Is it solving a real problem?
Would real people actually use this?
How well did you use AI to build it?

architect._note: one item per judging question, verbatim; delete unused items

muse.title: The Muse
muse.mission: Build the go-to-market strategy that gets families and partners using the service. Who's the audience? How do you reach them? What materials do you produce?

items.text: Do you understand who you're reaching?
Are channel choices realistic for the audience?
How well did you use AI for creative work?

muse._note: one item per judging question, verbatim; delete unused items

descriptors.Problem Understanding: Did they actually understand the problem? Do they know who the users/customers are and what they need? Or did they build something generic?
descriptors.Solution Quality: Is the solution good? Is the business plan sound? Is the product useful? Is the marketing strategy smart? Would this actually work?
descriptors.Presentation & Polish: Is it well-built and clearly presented? Can you interact with the dashboard? Does the plan read well? Are materials production-ready?
descriptors.Adaptability: How did they respond to the curveball? Did they rethink their approach or just bolt something on? (Score after Block 2)
descriptors.AI Mastery: How effectively did they use AI? Did they direct it or just accept first outputs? Evidence of iteration, challenging AI, using it creatively?

scoring.scale: circle one 1-5 per dimension per judge; TOTAL / 25 × 4 = / 100
scoring.notes: Adaptability is scored after Block 2; each judge adds 'What stood out? (one sentence)'; the panel is three industry experts and one non-human (AI) judge
scoring.source: Kansas_City_scorecard.png (KC Regional 2026 judge scorecard, March 28, 2026), read 2026-09-29; the same five dimensions appear on every 2026 brief
